mainTopic: The end of שמואל's exaggerations (the golden גפן and the פרוכת), and why olive and vine wood are not used on the מערכה.
overview: This amud finishes the sources for שמואל's statement that חכמים sometimes spoke in exaggerated language. People hung donated gold pieces on the golden vine, and moving it supposedly took three hundred כהנים. The פרוכת is described as huge and costly, and supposedly needed three hundred כהנים to immerse it. Then the גמרא returns to the משנה: any wood may go on the מערכה except olive and vine. רב פפא says these woods are knotty. רב אחא בר יעקב says using them would harm the settlement of ארץ ישראל. A ברייתא seems to challenge רב אחא בר יעקב, since the תנא קמא allows palm wood even though the palm is a valuable tree. The answer is that the fig and palm wood that was used came from trees that do not bear fruit. The גמרא then asks whether a fruitless fig really exists, and begins quoting רחבה about white figs; his statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Donors hang their gifts on the golden vine
steps.stepSummary: The source about the golden vine concludes: anyone who donated a leaf, a grape or a cluster would bring it and hang it on the vine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or a grape, or a cluster: the donor brings it and hangs it on the vine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote about the golden גפן at the entrance of the היכל. People would donate gold pieces shaped like vine parts and hang them on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line explains why the vine kept getting heavier over time. Every donor added more gold to it. That growing weight sets up the next line, which describes the exaggeration שמואל was talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: vine; here, the golden vine at the entrance of the היכל

phrases.english: or a grape, or a cluster —
phrases.notes: We're joining mid-sentence: whoever donated a gold leaf, grape or cluster for the golden vine…

phrases.english: brings it and hangs it on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ גַרְגִּיר, אוֹ אֶשְׁכּוֹל – מֵבִיא וְתוֹלֶה בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the source for שמואל's second exaggeration (the vine), which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Donated gold leaves, grapes and clusters were hung on the golden vine, so it grew heavier and heavier.

steps.title: Three hundred priests to move the vine
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק reports an incident in which three hundred כהנים were assigned to move the vine. This is the exaggeration שמואל referred to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק said: There was an incident, and three hundred priests were counted out to move the vine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the line that shows the exaggeration about the vine. It says moving the vine took three hundred כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vine really was very heavy, but not so heavy that three hundred people were needed. That is why שמואל counted this as גוזמא, an exaggerated way of speaking. Now שמואל's claim about the vine is backed by a source.

keyTerms.meaning: to move it or clear it away

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, said:
There was an incident,
and three hundred priests were counted out for it
to move it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק: מַעֲשֶׂה הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the vine source by giving the exaggerated detail.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's statement that the חכמים exaggerated about the vine
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק's report that three hundred כהנים were needed to move the vine

steps.title: The curtain's thickness and weave
steps.stepSummary: For the third exaggeration, the פרוכת, the גמרא quotes a משנה. It says the curtain was a טפח thick and woven from 72 strands, each made of 24 threads.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Curtain: as we learned, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says in the name of רבי שמעון הסגן: The Curtain is a handbreadth thick. It is woven from seventy-two strands, and each strand is made of twenty-four threads.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the source for שמואל's third exaggeration, the פרוכת. It starts by describing how thick the curtain was and how it was woven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives exact details about how thick the curtain was and how it was woven. These details build up a picture of an enormous, heavy curtain. The description continues in the next step, which reaches the detail שמואל counted as an exaggeration.

keyTerms.meaning: the Curtain in the בית המקדש
a strand (a cord made of several threads)

phrases.english: The Curtain —

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: as we learned: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says
in the name of Rabbi Shimon the deputy High Priest:
The Curtain's thickness is a handbreadth;
it is woven from seventy-two strands,
and for each and every strand
there are twenty-four threads.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּרוֹכֶת – דִּתְנַן רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הַסְּגָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the vine to the third exaggeration, the curtain.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's statement that the חכמים exaggerated about the פרוכת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the name of רבי שמעון הסגן

steps.title: The curtain's size, cost and weight
steps.stepSummary: The same משנה continues. The curtain was 40 by 20 אמות, cost 820,000, two were made every year, and three hundred כהנים were needed to immerse it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its length is forty cubits and its width twenty cubits. It is made at a cost of eighty-two ten-thousands, two are made every year, and three hundred priests immerse it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes describing the פרוכת: its size, its cost, how often it was made, and how many כהנים it took to immerse it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last detail, three hundred כהנים to immerse it, matches the vine's three hundred כהנים. This is the clear overstatement שמואל had in mind. With this, all three of שמואל's examples have their sources.

keyTerms.meaning: immerse (in a מקוה, to make it טהור)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's three exaggerations each have a source. The vine needed three hundred כהנים to move it, and the curtain needed three hundred כהנים to immerse it. These are overstatements, not literal numbers.

phrases.english: Its length is forty cubits,
and its width is twenty cubits.
And it is made from eighty-two ten-thousands,
and two are made each and every year,
and three hundred priests immerse it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אׇרְכָּהּ אַרְבָּעִים אַמָּה, וְרׇחְבָּהּ עֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה about the curtain and reaches the exaggerated detail.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ending of the משנה: three hundred כהנים immerse it

steps.title: Back to the משנה: no olive or vine wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to quoting our משנה. The כהנים began bringing up logs to build the wood pile, using any wood except olive and vine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: They began bringing up logs to arrange the wood pile, and so on. Any wood is fit except olive and vine, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to our משנה and quotes the rule about which wood may go on the מזבח. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא was on a side topic, שמואל's exaggerations. Here it returns to the main line of the משנה. It highlights the one exception: olive and vine wood are not used.

keyTerms.meaning: the arranged wood pile on the מזבח

phrases.english: They began bringing up the logs
to arrange the wood pile, etc.
except for olive wood and vine wood, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." just means the quote from the משנה keeps going; the גמרא only cites the opening words.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵחֵלּוּ מַעֲלִין בַּגְּזִירִין לְסַדֵּר אֶת הַמַּעֲרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion of exaggerations and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wood from any tree may be used for the מערכה except olive and vine.

steps.title: Why not olive and vine wood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why olive and vine wood are excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason for these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה excludes these two kinds of wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a rule without a reason. The גמרא wants to understand what makes these trees different, and two answers follow.

phrases.english: These, what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason olive and vine wood may not be used on the מערכה.

steps.title: רב פפא: the wood is knotty
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that these woods are full of knots.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Because they have knots.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that olive and vine wood are excluded because they are knotty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason is about the wood itself. Knotty wood does not burn well and makes a lot of smoke, so it is not suitable for the מזבח fire.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Because they are knotty.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wood has knots, so it is unfit for the fire.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: protecting the settlement of ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב gives a different reason: using these trees for firewood would harm the settlement of ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: Because of the settlement of ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב offers a second explanation: we avoid cutting down olive trees and vines because the land needs them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's reason was about how the wood burns. רב אחא בר יעקב's reason is about the people of the land: olives and grapes are important crops. Burning these trees on the מזבח would use them up and hurt יישוב ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: the settlement and prosperity of the Land of Israel

steps.whatToRemember: Olive and vine wood are not used on the מערכה. רב פפא says it is because they are knotty, and רב אחא בר יעקב says it is to protect יישוב ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
Because of the settlement of the Land of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם יִשּׁוּב דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the same question, using a different kind of reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Using these trees would deplete crops that the settlement of ארץ ישראל depends on.

steps.title: A ברייתא: altar wood must burn fully and be free of knots
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens an objection by quoting a ברייתא. It reads the פסוק to mean that altar wood must burn completely, like smooth branches with no knots inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises an objection. The פסוק says 'upon the wood that is on the fire.' This means wood that melts away until it becomes fire. What kind of wood is that? Smooth branches, straight like a skewer, that have no knots inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts an objection against רב אחא בר יעקב by quoting the first part of a ברייתא. This step sets up the challenge; the actual question comes in step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the ideal altar wood burns fully and has no knots inside. This fits well with רב פפא's reason, that olive and vine are excluded because of their knots. The ברייתא keeps going in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Smooth, straight branches, like a skewer

phrases.english: They raised an objection: 'Upon the wood that is on the fire'
wood that burns away until it becomes fire,
And what is that? Branches smooth like a skewer
that do not become knotted on the inside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test the two reasons given in steps 7 and 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's reason (the settlement of ארץ ישראל)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the ברייתא stresses that the wood should have no knots. The full attack comes in step 12.

steps.title: Which trees are fit for the altar fire
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: all trees are fit except olive and vine. The כהנים usually used fig, nut and pine, and רבי אליעזר adds more trees to the unfit list.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are all trees fit for the מערכה? All trees are fit except olive and vine. But the כהנים usually used these: young branches of fig, nut, and pine trees. רבי אליעזר adds: also hackberry, oak, palm, carob, and sycamore.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and lists which trees may be used for the altar fire. It also brings a disagreement between the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא rules out only olive and vine. רבי אליעזר rules out five more trees, including the palm (דקל). That means the תנא קמא allows palm wood, and the גמרא will use this point in step 12.
steps.confusionAlert: 'רבי אליעזר adds' does not mean he adds more fit trees. He adds more trees to the list of trees that may NOT be used.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי כׇּל הָעֵצִים כְּשֵׁרִים לַמַּעֲרָכָה הֵן?
phrases.english: And are all trees fit for the wood pile?

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָעֵצִים כְּשֵׁרִים, חוּץ מִן זַיִת וְגֶפֶן.
phrases.english: All trees are fit, except olive and vine.
But they were used to using these:

phrases.aramaic: בְּמֻרְבִּיּוֹת שֶׁל תְּאֵנָה, וְשֶׁל אֱגוֹז, וְשֶׁל עֵץ שֶׁמֶן.
phrases.english: young branches of fig, of nut, and of pine.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מוֹסִיף אַף שֶׁל מַיִישׁ, וְשֶׁל אַלּוֹן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer adds also hackberry, and oak,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל דֶּקֶל, וְשֶׁל חָרוּב, וְשֶׁל שִׁקְמָה.
phrases.english: and palm, and carob, and sycamore.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי כׇּל הָעֵצִים כְּשֵׁרִים לַמַּעֲרָכָה הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא quoted in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: Which trees may be used for the מערכה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: only olive and vine are excluded according to the תנא קמא; רבי אליעזר also excludes five more trees, including the palm.

steps.title: The knots reason explains the disagreement well
steps.stepSummary: If the problem is knots, the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר disagree about trees that are knotted only on the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says the reason is knots. They disagree about this: One opinion holds that even though these trees are not knotted inside, since they are knotted outside, we do not bring them. The other opinion holds that since they are not knotted inside, even though they are knotted outside, we do bring them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב פפא's reason (knots) explains the argument in the ברייתא well. This prepares the contrast with רב אחא בר יעקב in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's extra trees are knotted only on the outside, and he rules them out. The תנא קמא cares only about knots on the inside, so he allows them. With the knots reason, the ברייתא makes good sense.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for... (sets up a contrast with 'אלא')

phrases.english: It works well for the one who says it is because they are knotted,
they disagree about this:

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא קְטִרִי מִגַּוַּאי,
phrases.english: One master holds: even though they are not knotted inside,
since they are knotted outside, we do not bring them.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא קְטִרִי מִגַּוַּאי,
phrases.english: And the other master holds: since they are not knotted inside,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּמִבָּרַאי קְטִרִי – מַיְיתִינַן.
phrases.english: even though they are knotted outside, we do bring them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from steps 9-10 to show it fits רב פפא's reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: Sets up the contrast between רב פפא and רב אחא בר יעקב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Shows that one reason explains the ברייתא smoothly, so the other reason must also explain it. Step 12 shows that it does not.

steps.title: Isn't the palm tree also important to the Land?
steps.stepSummary: If olive and vine are excluded to protect ארץ ישראל, the palm should be excluded too. So why does the תנא קמא allow it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But for the one who says the reason is the settlement of ארץ ישראל: doesn't the palm tree also matter for the settlement of ארץ ישראל?
steps.whatsHappening: Here the גמרא delivers its actual challenge against רב אחא בר יעקב. His reason seems to say the palm should be banned, but the תנא קמא allows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא בר יעקב said olive and vine are excluded so the Land's important trees are not cut down. The palm is also a valuable tree of ארץ ישראל, yet the תנא קמא lets it be used. Steps 13 and 14 answer this challenge on his behalf.

keyTerms.meaning: But (turns to the side that has a problem)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא fits the knots reason (רב פפא) well. But the settlement reason (רב אחא בר יעקב) seems to clash with the תנא קמא, who allows palm wood.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם יִשּׁוּב דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.english: But for the one who says it is because of the settlement of the Land of Israel:
does the palm tree not have
the concern of the settlement of the Land of Israel?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם יִשּׁוּב דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא/אלא contrast that began in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's reason that olive and vine are excluded because of יישוב ארץ ישראל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The palm is also important for the Land, so his reason should exclude it. But the תנא קמא of the ברייתא allows palm wood.

steps.title: The same question applies to the fig tree
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב answers by turning the question around: the fig is also a valuable tree for ארץ ישראל, yet the כהנים used fig wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could say to you: By your logic, isn't the fig also a concern for the settlement of ארץ ישראל?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב answers the palm-tree question by showing that the fig raises the very same problem. This sets up his real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in step 10 said the כהנים usually burned fig wood, and the fig is an important fruit tree. So the palm is not a special problem for his reason. Whatever explains the fig will also explain the palm.

keyTerms.meaning: And by your own reasoning: turning the question back on the asker

phrases.english: He could say to you:
phrases.notes: "He" is רב אחא בר יעקב, answering the palm-tree question from step 12.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning:
doesn't the fig tree also have
the concern of the settlement of the Land of Israel?!
phrases.notes: Yet the ברייתא in step 10 said the כהנים usually used fig wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the palm-tree question of step 12 by showing the fig raises the same problem.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-question (ולטעמיך): the same problem exists in an accepted case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The palm seemed to be a special problem for רב אחא בר יעקב's reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fig has the same issue, so one answer will cover both trees.

steps.title: A fig or palm that does not bear fruit
steps.stepSummary: The answer for both trees: the wood that was allowed came from a fig or palm that does not produce fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? That it means a fig that does not bear fruit. The palm too means one that does not bear fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב gives his real answer. The fig and palm wood that was allowed came from trees that do not bear fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about ארץ ישראל is only about cutting down fruit-bearing trees. A tree that gives no fruit can be cut without harming the land. So his reason stands, and the palm question is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what must you say? The answer you are forced to give

steps.whatToRemember: רב אחא בר יעקב's reason stands: only fruit-bearing trees are protected. The fig and palm wood used on the מזבח came from trees that do not bear fruit.

phrases.english: Rather, what do you have to say?
It is about a fig that does not produce fruit,
the palm as well –
is about one that does not produce fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual answer that the counter-question of step 13 pointed toward.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): only fruitless trees
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Allowing the palm seemed to clash with protecting the trees of ארץ ישראל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The allowed fig and palm are fruitless kinds, so cutting them does no harm to the land.

steps.title: Is there really a fig that gives no fruit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a fig tree that bears no fruit actually exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is there such a thing as a fig that does not produce fruit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the answer from step 14 by asking whether a fruitless fig actually exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fig trees are known for giving fruit, so the answer only works if fruitless figs are real. If they are not, the answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But is there really such a thing?

phrases.english: But is there a fig tree
that does not produce fruit?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא תְּאֵנָה דְּלָא עָבְדָא פֵּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the case set up in step 14 exists in reality.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a fig tree that bears no fruit actually exists.

steps.title: Yes, like רחבה's white figs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes, based on what רחבה said about growing white figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, like רחבה, for רחבה said: They bring white figs...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that fruitless figs do exist and starts quoting רחבה as the source. His full statement continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רחבה describes a way of growing figs that starts with white figs. His statement will show that some fig trees really give no fruit, which supports step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: White figs, a kind of fig tree

phrases.english: Yes, as in the statement of Rachava.
